Table 8: Prompt templates for each personalization task. {USER PREFIX + RECORD PREFIX} denotes the combined prefix Pu,q = Pu + Pq, prepended as soft tokens (present only in TAP-PER; absent for all other methods). {USER_PROFILE} is a natural language summary of user preferences (present only in PAG variants). {USER_HISTORY} contains the top-k retrieved records (present only in RAG variants). Each placeholder and its surrounding section header are included only when the corresponding component is active; otherwise the entire block is omitted.

Figure 4: Storage and time scaling comparison. Top: total parameter count as a function of user population. Bottom: per-user training time as a function of history length on LaMP-2M; the dashed green line denotes the TAP-PER variant without user-state prefix Pu, which requires no per-user gradient updates.

Figure 3: Case study on a representative query from LaMP-2M. The non-personalized baseline and the temporal-free TAP-PER variant predict incorrect tags, whereas the full TAP-PER correctly identifies the ground-truth tag by attending to recent query-relevant records. Darker red indicates higher attention weight.
Table 7: Comparison results on LaMP benchmark with Qwen3-4B as backbone. Notation follows Table 1.

Figure 2: Overview of TAP-PER’s personalized prefix learning. With the task-adapted backbone θtask frozen, a user-state prefix Pu is fetched from a per-user embedding table and a query-aware record prefix Pq is produced by temporal-decayed attention over the user’s full interaction history. The two are summed and prepended to the query, while a shared bridge LoRA ∆θbridge is jointly trained to deeply condition the backbone on the prefix signals. Stage 1 (task-level LoRA adaptation) precedes this stage and is omitted from the diagram.

Figure 6: Online adaptation to streaming feedback on LaMP-2M (top) and LaMP-5 (bottom). x-axis: fraction of training history absorbed (50% = bootstrap, 60–100% = after each of the five streaming chunks); y-axis: testset metric.

Table 1: Comparison results on LaMP benchmark across prompt-based and model-based personalization. Bold and underline denote the best and second-best result per metric, respectively. k denotes the number of retrieved items, with k=0 indicating no retrieval. ↑ indicates higher is better; ↓ indicates lower is better. For OPPU and PER-PCS, the columns are cumulative: +rag adds RAG on top of base, and +pag further adds PAG on top of +rag. For P2P, single denotes the single hypernetwork-generated LoRA variant without retrieval or profile stacking. For TAP-PER: †base = task-adapted model (Stage 1 only); ‡+Pq = adding query-aware record prefix; §+Pu = further adding user-state prefix (full model). The Pq and Pu columns parallel the +rag and +pag columns of OPPU/PER-PCS, as they serve analogous roles through learned prefix representations.
Table 9: Qualitative output comparison. ✓ marks a correct answer and ✗ an incorrect one.
